1	# Global Airport Performance Dataset
     2	
     3	## Overview
     4	This dataset contains operational performance metrics for 30 major international airports worldwide, covering passenger throughput, on-time performance, and route network size across six geographic regions.
     5	
     6	## Data Source
     7	
     8	### airports
     9	Each record represents one airport with the following fields:
    10	- **airport** (string): Airport name with IATA code in parentheses
    11	- **throughput_million** (float): Annual passenger throughput in millions of passengers, ranging from ~10 to ~94
    12	- **on_time_rate** (float): On-time departure/arrival performance as a percentage, ranging from ~70% to ~91%
    13	- **routes** (integer): Number of active airline routes served, ranging from 95 to 370
    14	- **region** (string): Geographic region — one of North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific, Middle East, Latin America, or Africa
    15	
    16	## Data Notes
    17	- Throughput figures are approximate annual totals representative of recent pre-pandemic or recovery-period levels
    18	- On-time rate is a blended metric combining departure and arrival punctuality
    19	- Route counts reflect unique city-pair connections and may vary seasonally; figures represent peak-season snapshots
    20	- Three airports are designated for annotation: Atlanta (highest throughput), Dubai (mega-hub with high throughput), and Tokyo Haneda (highest on-time rate)

import json
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.cm as cm
import numpy as np

# Load data
with open('/app/benchmark/source_data.json', 'r') as f:
    data = json.load(f)

airports = data['airports']['data']

# Region to color mapping - professional business palette
region_colors = {
    'North America': '#2E5C8A',    # Deep blue
    'Europe': '#C44E52',            # Muted red
    'Asia-Pacific': '#55A868',      # Green
    'Middle East': '#CC7A00',       # Amber
    'Latin America': '#8172B2',     # Purple
    'Africa': '#6B8E8A'             # Teal
}

# Prepare data
regions = sorted(set(a['region'] for a in airports))
x = [a['throughput_million'] for a in airports]
y = [a['on_time_rate'] for a in airports]
sizes = [a['routes'] for a in airports]
colors = [region_colors[a['region']] for a in airports]

# Scale bubble sizes for visibility (area proportional to routes)
min_routes = min(sizes)
max_routes = max(sizes)
# Use a scaling that makes differences clear but keeps bubbles visible
scaled_sizes = [(r / max_routes) * 1200 + 80 for r in sizes]

# Create figure
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 9), facecolor='#FAFAFA')
ax.set_facecolor('#FAFAFA')

# Plot each region separately for proper legend
for region in regions:
    xs = [a['throughput_million'] for a in airports if a['region'] == region]
    ys = [a['on_time_rate'] for a in airports if a['region'] == region]
    ss = [(a['routes'] / max_routes) * 1200 + 80 for a in airports if a['region'] == region]
    ax.scatter(xs, ys, s=ss, c=region_colors[region], alpha=0.75,
               edgecolors='white', linewidths=1.2, label=region, zorder=3)

# Add subtle grid
ax.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.35, color='#999999', zorder=0)
ax.set_axisbelow(True)

# Axis labels and title
ax.set_xlabel('Annual Passenger Throughput (millions)', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold', color='#333333')
ax.set_ylabel('On-Time Performance (%)', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold', color='#333333')
ax.set_title('Airport Throughput vs. On-Time Performance Across 30 Major International Airports',
             fontsize=15, fontweight='bold', color='#1A1A1A', pad=18)

# Axis limits with padding
ax.set_xlim(5, 100)
ax.set_ylim(66, 95)

# Tick styling
ax.tick_params(axis='both', labelsize=11, colors='#444444')

# Spine styling
for spine in ax.spines.values():
    spine.set_color('#CCCCCC')
    spine.set_linewidth(0.8)

# Legend
legend = ax.legend(loc='lower left', fontsize=10, frameon=True,
                   fancybox=True, shadow=False, edgecolor='#CCCCCC',
                   facecolor='white', framealpha=0.92,
                   title='Region', title_fontsize=11)
legend.get_title().set_fontweight('bold')
legend.get_title().set_color('#333333')

# Annotate the three highlighted airports
annotations = {
    'Atlanta (ATL)': {'text': 'Atlanta (ATL)\nHighest throughput\n93.7M | 370 routes', 'offset': (18, 10)},
    'Dubai (DXB)': {'text': 'Dubai (DXB)\nMega-hub\n87.0M | 350 routes', 'offset': (18, -22)},
    'Tokyo Haneda (HND)': {'text': 'Tokyo Haneda (HND)\nHighest on-time rate\n68.9M | 230 routes', 'offset': (18, 8)}
}

for a in airports:
    name = a['airport']
    if name in annotations:
        info = annotations[name]
        ax.annotate(
            info['text'],
            xy=(a['throughput_million'], a['on_time_rate']),
            xytext=(a['throughput_million'] + info['offset'][0], a['on_time_rate'] + info['offset'][1]),
            fontsize=9,
            fontweight='bold',
            color='#1A1A1A',
            bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.4', facecolor='#FFF9E6', edgecolor='#D4A017', alpha=0.95, linewidth=1.2),
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color='#D4A017', lw=1.2,
                            connectionstyle='arc3,rad=0.1'),
            zorder=5
        )

# Add size legend for bubble sizes (route counts)
size_legend_values = [100, 200, 300, 370]
size_legend_sizes = [(v / max_routes) * 1200 + 80 for v in size_legend_values]

# Create size legend manually
size_legend_ax = fig.add_axes([0.82, 0.18, 0.12, 0.22])
size_legend_ax.set_xlim(0, 10)
size_legend_ax.set_ylim(0, len(size_legend_values) + 1)
size_legend_ax.axis('off')
size_legend_ax.set_title('Routes', fontsize=10, fontweight='bold', color='#333333', pad=8)

for i, (val, sz) in enumerate(zip(size_legend_values, size_legend_sizes)):
    y_pos = len(size_legend_values) - i
    size_legend_ax.scatter(2, y_pos, s=sz, c='#888888', alpha=0.75, edgecolors='white', linewidths=1.2)
    size_legend_ax.text(4.5, y_pos, f'{val}', va='center', ha='left', fontsize=9, color='#444444')

# Add footnote
fig.text(0.12, 0.02,
         'Bubble area ∝ number of routes. Data: approximate annual pre-pandemic/recovery-period levels.',
         fontsize=9, color='#888888', style='italic')

plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.04, 0.78, 1])

# Save
plt.savefig('/app/output/result.png', dpi=200, bbox_inches='tight', facecolor='#FAFAFA', edgecolor='none')
plt.close()
print("Saved to /app/output/result.png")
